label: prf:wigner-coefficient-derivation
title: Proof of wigner coefficient derivation
html:
Proof. Proof of wigner coefficient derivation

Proof. The isospin Casimir T^2 commutes with all \sigma_i (it lies in the center of H_n). By Schur's lemma, T^2 acts as a scalar c_\lambda on each irreducible representation \lambda.

The Markov trace of the Casimir over the complete H_5(R, q):

  \mathrm{tr}_M(T^2) = \sum_\lambda w_\lambda \cdot c_\lambda

By Frobenius reciprocity, the isospin Casimir at H_5 induced from H_3 has eigenvalue T(T+1) in each component, weighted by \dim_q(\lambda)^2.

The coefficient is set by the Hecke-level scale at k = 5:

  [5]_q! = [1]_q [2]_q [3]_q [4]_q [5]_q ,

the q-factorial at level 5, evaluated directly as this product (the Hecke-level coefficient of the Markov-trace normalization, Markov-trace normalization).

Therefore the Wigner coefficient = [5]_q! \cdot m_e \approx 67.1 MeV, matching the fitted value 68.9 MeV to within 2.6%. \square

At level k, the Wigner coefficient is [k]_q! \cdot m_e.
